items.title: Where Backtests and Live Trading Part Ways: Six Defects from One Intraday System
items.claim: In one intraday US equity system, every backtest-live drift traced to two paths that should agree but had drifted apart.

items.title: What does a Rejection Mean? A Retrospective Audit of a Registered Trading-rule Archive
items.claim: Of 23 nominal exclusions among 210 rejected rules, 22 survive a training-series re-verification, yet all carry secondary stopping failures.

items.title: When Judges Agree and Are Wrong: Consistency-Accuracy Dissociation as a Blind Spot for Label-Free Evaluation
items.claim: On four financial QA datasets, 60% of wrong answers sit in high-consistency regions, so agreement-based label-free evaluation misses confident errors.

items.title: How Much Screening Buys a Second? Speed, Selection, and the Maker's Spread
items.claim: A twelve-second maker must screen at least 84.5% of informed flow to match a one-second venue, versus 71.1% under a Gaussian model.

items.title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
items.claim: Moving from call-start to completion proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of 552 earnings calls, so labels depend on the declared outcome clock.
